title: RideLink Long-Distance Stays — Nights Added for Early and Late Appointments (Training Q&A)
content:
On a Non-Emergency Medical Transportation long-distance stay, the number of lodging nights depends not only on the appointment dates but on the appointment times.

**Rule.** The lodging nights also take in the nights the appointment times need: when the outbound leg's appointment starts before the early-start time of 09:00 and the return leg's appointment starts at or after the late-finish time of 15:00, the night before the first appointment and the night after the last are added to the nights between the two appointment dates; when exactly one of those two holds, the one night it needs is added; when neither holds, only the nights between the two appointment dates count.

The appointment times are the times registered on the trip's outbound leg and return leg.

## Combinations

| Outbound appointment starts before 09:00 | Return appointment starts at or after 15:00 | Nights added to the nights between the dates |
|---|---|---|
| Yes | Yes | 2 (the night before the first appointment and the night after the last) |
| Yes | No | 1 (the night before the first appointment) |
| No | Yes | 1 (the night after the last appointment) |
| No | No | None |

## Questions answered by the rule

- **Does an outbound appointment at exactly 09:00 add a night?** No. Only an appointment starting before 09:00 does; 08:59 does, 09:00 does not.
- **Does a return appointment at exactly 15:00 add a night?** Yes. An appointment starting at or after 15:00 does; 14:59 does not.
- **What are the lodging nights for an outbound appointment at 08:00 on 10 March and a return appointment at 16:00 on 13 March?** *Hypothetical:* 3 nights lie between the dates, and both times qualify, so the lodging nights are 5.
- **And for 10:30 on 10 March and 15:30 on 13 March?** *Hypothetical:* only the return time qualifies, so the lodging nights are 4.
